summary: The owner cannot see the business in one place: the staff job list has no counts, no costs and no company answers, billable events exist only as lines inside each job, and production holds one company record and zero introductions. The money guard that proves no rented machine is left running has failed every run since 2026-11-13 on retired RunPod and is filed as history in a 135 KB status whose red lists are otherwise dead experiments. Several manual steps protect nothing (a deploy window broken 100 times in 18 days, hand-recorded sends and answers, a success-threshold confirmation that changes no threshold), while two that protect privacy and money (withdrawal deletion approval, state backup) were never switched on. Approving a company is seven steps across Slack, a sign-in and two browser dialogs and should be one press from an email.

findings.today: The GPU spend guard, the unit that proves no rented machine is left running, exits 2 on every run because the RunPod inventory query fails. RunPod was retired on 2026-11-05. The failure posts to the alert route about once an hour, so the one alarm that protects money has been crying wolf since 2026-11-13. The door status lists the unit under historical diagnostics, beside 206 dead experiments.
findings.should: The guard is green when nothing is wrong, so a red guard means money is at risk.
findings.proposal: Drop RunPod from the guard's required providers (or remove the RunPod key from the host), so a retired provider is recorded as retired, not as a failed inventory. One small Pipeline PR plus one owner action on the host secret.
findings.user_result: The owner and operator see a green money guard, and its next red means a real orphaned machine.
findings.risk: If a RunPod resource still existed it would no longer be reaped; RunPod billing collection already stopped, so confirm the RunPod account is empty once in its console first.
findings.requirement_source: Money hard stop (owner, spend limits table in pipeline AGENTS.md); RunPod retirement 2026-11-05

findings.title: The alarm itself is fragile: the capacity controller was killed for memory seven times and state backup is not configured
evidence: cmd: door cat .../unit-failures/blueprint-control-plane-capacity.service.json -> oom-kill, failure_count 7, 2026-11-13..2026-11-20

findings.today: The unit that runs every stall check and posts every alert was OOM-killed seven times this month. The control-plane state backup check reports 'not_configured', so a lost host loses the job state the runbook's rebuild section relies on.
findings.should: The alarm runs in a protected memory slot and backups run and are checked.
findings.proposal: Give the capacity controller its own MemoryMin or move it out of contention; configure the state backup timer (owner decision if it costs storage).
findings.user_result: Alerts arrive when they should; a host loss is survivable.
findings.risk: Backup storage costs money (small); owner to approve the bucket.
findings.requirement_source: Runbook 'Control-plane state backup and host rebuild' (pipeline beta-operations.md:1181)
